text: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land where you are to live, which I am giving you,

and you present to the LORD an offering by fire from the herd or the flock—a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed festivals—to make a pleasing aroma for the LORD,
then the one who brings his offering shall present to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
With the burnt offering or the sacrifice you shall prepare a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering for each lamb.
For a ram you shall prepare a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,
and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Present it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a fellowship offering to the LORD,
a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil shall be brought with the bull,
and you shall bring half a hin of wine as a drink offering—an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
This is what shall be done for each bull, each ram, or each young sheep or goat.

versions.text: This is what shall be done for each bull, each ram, each male lamb, or each young goat.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has one category, שֶׂה (a single animal of the flock) further defined as "among the sheep or among the goats." The translation turns this into two separate animals and adds "male," which is not in the text.

text: Whatever the number you prepare, do this for each one, according to their number.
Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when he presents an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

And if a foreigner is staying with you, or whoever lives among you throughout your generations, and he wishes to present an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he shall do exactly as you do.
For the assembly there shall be one statute for you and for the foreigner who resides with you—a lasting statute for all your generations. Before the LORD, you and the foreigner shall be alike.
The same law and the same regulation shall apply both to you and to the foreigner residing among you.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,
and you eat the food of that land, you shall present a contribution to the LORD.
From the first of your dough you shall present a loaf as a contribution; present it like the contribution from the threshing floor.
Throughout your generations you shall give the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough.
Now if you stray unintentionally and fail to keep all these commands that the LORD gave Moses—
everything the LORD commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and onward through your generations—

then if it was done unintentionally, unnoticed by the congregation, the whole congregation shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, along with its prescribed grain offering and drink offering, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, and they will be forgiven, for it was unintentional and they have brought their offering to the LORD—an offering by fire and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional wrong.
The whole congregation of Israel will be forgiven, along with the foreigner residing among them, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
If a single person sins unintentionally, he shall bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who erred by sinning unintentionally, and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
You shall have one law for the native-born Israelite and for the foreigner residing among you, for anyone who sins unintentionally.
But the person who acts defiantly, whether native-born or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD; that person shall be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken his command, that person shall surely be cut off; his guilt remains on him.
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation,
and they kept him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him outside the camp."
So the whole congregation took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout their generations they are to make tassels on the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.

These tassels will be yours to look at, so that you may remember all the commands of the LORD and keep them, and not go chasing after your own heart and your own eyes, being unfaithful as you follow them.

versions.text: These tassels will be yours to look at, so that you may remember all the commands of the LORD and keep them, and not go chasing after your own heart and your own eyes, which lead you into unfaithfulness.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew makes the people the agents of the unfaithfulness ("after which you prostitute yourselves"); the current wording shifts the agency to the heart and eyes, softening the accusation.

text: So that you will remember and keep all my commands and be holy to your God.

versions.text: Then you will remember and keep all my commands and be holy to your God.
versions.explanation: לְמַעַן introduces a purpose clause ("in order that"), not a simple consequence; "Then" loses the purpose sense that ties this verse to the tassels.

text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.
